Year-to-date revenue increases 13.4%, gross margin improves to 67.9%, and interest expense declines 90%.

West Palm Beach, FL, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- QHSLab, Inc. (the “Company”) (OTCQB: USAQ), an SEC-reporting healthcare technology and software-as-a-service (SaaS) company whose annual financial statements are independently audited, today provided a shareholder update regarding its financial performance for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the continued evolution of its business, and management’s operational and strategic priorities as the Company approaches 2027.

Dear Shareholders,

While much of our communication is shaped by SEC reporting requirements, I wanted to take the time to write to you personally and share my perspective on where we are as a business and where we are heading.

Following the filing of our quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the period ended September 30, 2026, I wanted to provide our shareholders with additional perspective on our financial performance, the continued evolution of our business, and management’s priorities as we approach 2027.

During the first nine months of 2026, we continued to make progress in transitioning QHSLab toward a scalable, technology-enabled healthcare services business. While we achieved meaningful growth in our Integrated Service Program (ISP) and improved our gross margins, we also experienced a decline in our allergy diagnostics and immunotherapy business, increased operating expenses and greater demands on our available cash resources.

Year-to-Date 2026 Financial Highlights

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared with the corresponding period in 2025, the Company reported the following unaudited financial results:

  • Total revenue increased 13.4% to $2,253,347, compared with $1,987,931.
  • ISP revenue increased 63.9% to $1,287,692, compared with $785,506.
  • Gross profit increased 15.6% to $1,529,050, compared with $1,322,590.
  • Gross margin improved to 67.9%, compared with 66.5%.
  • Interest expense decreased 90.0% to $19,482, compared with $194,894.
  • Net loss totaled $119,021, compared with a net loss of $99,156.

Continued Growth of Our Integrated Service Program

Our ISP remains the principal driver of revenue growth and an important component of our long-term business strategy.

During the first nine months of 2026, ISP revenue increased by $502,186, representing year-over-year growth of 63.9%. More importantly, ISP now accounts for approximately 57% of our total revenue, compared with approximately 40% during the corresponding period in 2025.

This change in revenue composition reflects the continued evolution of QHSLab toward a software-enabled healthcare services business built around ongoing relationships with medical practices.

During the third quarter of 2026, ISP revenue increased 17.4% year-over-year to $421,792. While the rate of growth moderated compared with the first half of the year, the program continued to expand its contribution to our overall business.

We remain focused on acquiring new medical practice customers, increasing utilization among existing customers, expanding our portfolio of digital healthcare services, and improving the operational efficiency and scalability of our service delivery model.

Allergy Diagnostics and Immunotherapy Treatment

Combined revenue from allergy diagnostic kit sales and immunotherapy treatment decreased 19.3% to $828,854 during the first nine months of 2026, compared with $1,027,611 during the corresponding period in 2025.

The decline was more pronounced during the third quarter, with combined allergy-related revenue decreasing 37.0%, reflecting lower purchasing activity among certain existing physician customers. As a result, despite continued ISP revenue growth, total third-quarter revenue decreased 8.1% to $677,172.

In September 2026, we implemented changes to our supplier arrangements that are expected to reduce the cost of our allergy diagnostic kits by approximately 10% to 13%, based on historical sales volumes and product mix. These changes are intended to improve the profitability of future allergy diagnostic kit sales.

Management remains focused on improving the commercial and financial performance of this established business line.

Gross Margins, Operating Expenses and Profitability

Despite the decline in allergy-related revenue, our overall gross margin improved to 67.9% for the first nine months of 2026, compared with 66.5% during the corresponding period in 2025.

For the nine-month period, gross profit increased by $206,460, or 15.6%, compared with the prior year. However, total operating expenses increased by $401,737, or 32.7%, principally reflecting increased personnel, sales and marketing expenditures, corporate insurance and administrative costs.

Research and development expenditures decreased approximately 5% to $350,604, while we continued to enhance our proprietary technology platform and expand our healthcare service capabilities.

The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into our engineering and software development processes is improving development efficiency, accelerating product enhancements and enabling us to scale our technology platform without a corresponding increase in development expenditures.

We are increasingly realizing the benefits of our historical investments in technology, software architecture and clinical intellectual property. Our existing technology infrastructure and engineering resources are currently sufficient to support our planned platform enhancements, expansion of healthcare service capabilities and growth in customer utilization.

While the full commercial and financial benefits of these developments are not yet reflected in our revenue and earnings, management believes we are establishing a more capital-efficient and scalable business model. Our technology platform is designed to accommodate a substantially larger customer base without requiring proportionate increases in development expenditure.

As we approach 2027, our focus is increasingly shifting toward commercial execution, customer acquisition, utilization and generating financial returns from the technology and operational infrastructure we have established.

We believe this represents an important stage in the evolution of QHSLab as we work toward sustainable profitability and positive operating cash flow.

Management recognizes the need to improve operating leverage by generating additional revenue from the technology, personnel and operational infrastructure already established within the business. Our priority is to translate future revenue growth into improved operating profitability and positive cash flow.

Liquidity and Capital Resources

During the past twelve months, we substantially reduced our outstanding debt obligations and associated financing costs. Interest expense for the first nine months of 2026 declined by approximately $175,000 compared with the corresponding period in 2025.

As of September 30, 2026, the Company reported:

  • Cash and cash equivalents of $190,464.
  • Net accounts receivable of $308,923.
  • Total current assets of $519,108.
  • Total current liabilities of $247,114.
  • Positive working capital of $271,994.
  • No outstanding long-term liabilities.

Total liabilities decreased approximately 54.7%, from $546,078 at December 31, 2025, to $247,114 at September 30, 2026.

Cash decreased by $445,693 during the first nine months of 2026, reflecting approximately $335,000 used in operating activities and $111,000 used in financing activities related to debt repayment. This compares with approximately $80,000 generated from operating activities during the corresponding period in 2025. Operating cash flow during 2026 was impacted by operating losses, increased accounts receivable and a reduction in outstanding accounts payable.

Management remains focused on improving cash collections, managing operating expenditures and increasing the contribution of ongoing service-based revenues to operating cash flow.

While the reduction in debt has lowered financing costs, improving liquidity remains an important priority. As disclosed in our Form 10-Q, substantial doubt remains regarding the Company's ability to continue as a going concern. Our ability to continue operations depends upon achieving sustainable positive operating cash flow or obtaining additional financing, if necessary.

Our objective remains to increasingly support the business through internally generated cash flow.

Management's Focus as We Approach 2027

As we approach 2027, our operational priorities remain clear:

  • Expand our network of medical practice customers and accelerate customer activation.
  • Increase ongoing service revenue through greater utilization of ISP among new and existing customers.
  • Commercialize additional software-enabled healthcare programs using our existing technology infrastructure.
  • Improve the commercial and financial performance of our allergy diagnostics and treatment business.
  • Generate greater operating leverage from our existing technology, personnel and administrative infrastructure.
  • Improve cash collections, expenditure management and operating efficiency.
  • Work toward sustainable operating profitability and positive cash flow.

We believe the progress we have made in developing our technology platform, expanding our healthcare service capabilities and reducing our financing costs provides a foundation for the next stage of our business development.

Management Commentary

“Building a sustainable healthcare technology company requires us to remain focused on the fundamentals of our business. We are encouraged by the continued growth of our Integrated Service Program and its increasing contribution to our overall revenue. At the same time, we recognize that revenue growth alone is not enough. We must translate that growth into improved operating profitability and positive cash flow,” said Troy Grogan, President and Chief Executive Officer of QHSLab.

“Our priorities are to grow revenue, improve the performance of our allergy diagnostics and treatment business, exercise greater discipline over operating expenditures, and generate improved financial returns from the technology and operational infrastructure we have established.

“An important development that may not yet be fully apparent in our financial results is the increasing scalability of our technology and the productivity of our engineering team. We are developing more capabilities, expanding our healthcare service offerings and improving our platform without increasing our research and development expenditures. Our challenge and opportunity now is to translate these capabilities into greater customer adoption, revenue growth and improved earnings. We are focused on building a commercially sustainable healthcare technology business through disciplined investment and responsible capital allocation.”

“We recognize the importance of shareholder value and appreciate the confidence our shareholders have placed in management. While short-term fluctuations in our share price are not within management's direct control, we remain focused on the factors we can influence: the quality of our products and services, customer growth and retention, operating efficiency, responsible capital allocation and financial performance.

“As we approach 2027, our focus is increasingly on converting the progress we have made in building our business into sustainable financial performance. We believe that executing on these fundamentals is the most meaningful way to work toward creating long-term shareholder value.”

On behalf of our entire team, I would like to thank our shareholders for their continued support and interest in QHSLab.

Sincerely,

Troy Grogan
President and Chief Executive Officer
QHSLab, Inc. (OTCQB: USAQ)

Financial results included in this release are unaudited. Shareholders are encouraged to review the Company’s complete quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the period ended September 30, 2026, filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on November 12, 2026.

For additional information, including the Company’s latest corporate presentation, please visit the QHSLab investor relations website at https://www.qhslab.com/for-investors.

About QHSLab, Inc.

QHSLab, Inc. (OTCQB: USAQ) is an SEC-reporting healthcare technology company focused on improving preventive and value-based care through digital health solutions and point-of-care services. The Company provides healthcare organizations with technology-enabled programs designed to identify patient health risks, support clinical decision-making, improve patient engagement, and create new opportunities for practice revenue.

QHSLab files periodic reports with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, and its annual financial statements are subject to independent audit. The Company is focused on disciplined growth, financial transparency and expanding its portfolio of healthcare solutions for medical practices and their patients.

For more information, visit QHSLab.com.

Forward-Looking Statements

This press release contains forward-looking statements regarding the Company’s business strategy, anticipated revenue growth, operating efficiency, expected cost reductions, liquidity, product development and future financial performance.

These statements reflect management’s current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially, including changes in healthcare reimbursement policies, customer adoption and retention, demand for the Company’s products and services, operating expenses, collection of accounts receivable, availability of additional financing and the Company’s ability to achieve sustainable profitability and positive operating cash flow.

Additional information concerning these and other risks is contained in the Company’s periodic filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

Forward-looking statements speak only as of the date of this release. The Company undertakes no obligation to update these statements except as required by applicable law.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- NeuroSense Therapeutics Ltd. (NASDAQ: NRSN) ("NeuroSense"), a late-stage clinical biotechnology company focused on developing disease-modifying treatments for neurodegenerative diseases, today announced that Chief Financial Officer Or Eisenberg will participate in the 9th Annual Evercore Healthcare Conference, taking place from November 30 to December 2, 2026, at the Loews Coral Gables Hotel in Coral Gables, Florida.

Mr. Eisenberg will participate in a fireside chat hosted by Michael DiFiore, Evercore ISI research analyst, on Monday, November 30, at 3:00 p.m. ET, and will be available for one-on-one meetings with institutional investors during the conference. Discussions are expected to focus on the Company's recent clinical and regulatory progress with PrimeC, its lead drug candidate for the treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), as well as the Company's development strategy and regulatory plans for PrimeC in Canada, the U.S. and other key markets.

About NeuroSense

NeuroSense Therapeutics is a late-clinical stage biotechnology company developing novel treatments for severe neurodegenerative diseases, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and Alzheimer's disease. The Company's lead product candidate, PrimeC, is a novel oral therapy designed to target multiple key biological pathways underlying disease progression, including neuroinflammation, oxidative stress and dysregulated iron metabolism.

NeuroSense has recently completed analysis of long-term follow-up data from its Phase 2b PARADIGM study in ALS, with results published in JAMA Neurology showing slowing of functional decline relative to placebo. The Company also reported changes across multiple biomarkers associated with ALS, including microRNAs, consistent with PrimeC's multi-target mechanism of action.

The Company has received clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to initiate its pivotal Phase 3 PARAGON trial in ALS and is working with the FDA on an optimized study design.

For additional information, we invite you to visit our website and follow us on LinkedIn, YouTube and X. Information that may be important to investors may be routinely posted on our website and these social media channels.

About PrimeC

PrimeC, NeuroSense's lead drug candidate, is a novel extended-release oral formulation composed of a unique fixed-dose combination of two FDA-approved drugs: ciprofloxacin and celecoxib. PrimeC is designed to target several key mechanisms that contribute to neuron degeneration, inflammation, iron accumulation and impaired ribonucleic acid ("RNA") regulation, with the potential to inhibit disease progression.

About ALS

Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis ("ALS") is an incurable neurodegenerative disease that causes complete paralysis and death within 3 years from diagnosis. Every year, more than 5,000 people are diagnosed with ALS in the U.S. alone, with an annual disease burden of $1 billion. The number of people living with ALS is expected to grow by 24% by 2040 in the U.S. and EU.

HSINCHU, Taiwan--(BUSINESS WIRE)--SemiLEDs Corporation (NASDAQ: LEDS), “SemiLEDs” or the “Company,” a developer and manufacturer of LED chips and LED components, today announced its financial results for the fourth quarter and full fiscal year 2026, ended August 31, 2026.

Revenue for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 was $6.4 million, compared to $9.1 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2026. GAAP net income attributable to SemiLEDs stockholders for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 was $640 thousand, or $0.08 per diluted share, compared to a net income of $1.5 million, or $0.18 per diluted share, in the third quarter of fiscal 2026.

GAAP gross margin for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 decreased to 23%, compared to 27% for the third quarter of fiscal 2026. Operating margin for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 decreased to 7%, compared to 16% for the third quarter of fiscal 2026. The Company’s cash and cash equivalents were $4.6 million at August 31, 2026, compared to $6.0 million at the end of the third quarter of fiscal 2026.

Revenues for fiscal year 2026 decreased to $19.1 million, compared to $43.0 million in fiscal year 2025. GAAP net income attributable to SemiLEDs stockholders for fiscal year 2026 was $817 thousand, or $0.10 per diluted share, compared to a net loss of $1.1 million, or $(0.15) per diluted share, in fiscal year 2025.

GAAP gross margin for fiscal year 2026 increased to 21%, compared to 6% for fiscal year 2025. Operating margin for fiscal year 2026 was 0.1%, compared to negative 4% in fiscal year 2025. The Company’s cash and cash equivalents were $4.6 million as of August 31, 2026, compared to $2.6 million as of August 31, 2025.

In fiscal years 2026 and 2025, the Company entered into a number of buy-sell orders for equipment that it purchased and then sold to its customers, and the Company anticipates continuing to receive buy-sell purchase orders in fiscal year 2027. As a result of these purchase orders and the associated uncertainty of the business, the Company’s revenue, cost of revenues, receivables, inventories and customer deposits may vary significantly over future quarters.

About SemiLEDs

SemiLEDs develops, manufactures, and sells light emitting diode (LED) chips, LED components, LED modules, sensor components incorporating LED or vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL), and systems. Its products are used for general lighting and specialty industrial applications, including ultraviolet, or UV, curing of polymers, LED light therapy in medical/cosmetic applications, counterfeit detection, germicidal and virucidal devices, LED lighting for horticulture applications, architectural lighting, entertainment lighting, and sensing of pressure or distance using LED or VCSEL.

gaapfinancial
GAAP, or Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, are a set of standardized rules and guidelines that companies follow when preparing their financial statements. They ensure consistency, transparency, and comparability across different companies, making it easier for investors to understand and compare financial information accurately. This helps investors make informed decisions based on trustworthy and uniform financial reports.

vcseltechnical
A VCSEL is a tiny semiconductor laser that emits light straight out of the surface of a chip, like a miniature, very precise flashlight built into an electronic component. Investors care because VCSELs are key parts in optical communication, sensors, and proximity or gesture controls—products with growing demand—so changes in VCSEL supply, cost or adoption can affect a maker’s sales, margins and the competitive position of companies that rely on them.
accounts receivablefinancial
Money a company is owed by its customers for goods or services already delivered but not yet paid for. Think of it like a stack of IOUs or open tabs: it represents future cash the business expects to collect. Investors watch accounts receivable because large or growing balances can signal strong sales or potential cash shortfalls if customers don’t pay, affecting liquidity, working capital and the company’s financial health.
noncontrolling interestsfinancial
The portion of a subsidiary’s equity and profits that belongs to outside owners rather than the parent company; when a parent reports consolidated results it includes the whole subsidiary but shows the noncontrolling slice separately. Think of a company’s subsidiary as a pie where the parent owns most slices but some are held by other investors — noncontrolling interests tell you how much of the pie and its future earnings don’t belong to the parent, which affects how much profit and net assets are truly attributable to the parent’s shareholders.

CHICAGO, IL / ACCESS Newswire / November 27, 2026 / Cosmos Health Inc. ("Cosmos Health" or the "Company") (NASDAQ:COSM), a diversified, vertically integrated global healthcare group, today announced a Facility Master Plan to expand and modernize the manufacturing facility and warehouse of its wholly owned subsidiary, Cana Laboratories S.A. ("Cana"), in Athens, Greece. The first phase, comprising a new quality control laboratory and a new GMP warehouse, commences this quarter and is targeted for completion by the third quarter of 2027.

Strategic Rationale

Cana's contract manufacturing business continues to grow. Its contract manufacturing pipeline now exceeds 32.7 million units, Cana inaugurated a new capsule-filling production line in June 2026, and the Company recently announced the addition of an automated tablet coating system. The Master Plan is designed to ensure that Cana's infrastructure keeps pace with this growth and continues to meet applicable regulatory standards.

The program is structured across ten workstreams, each with defined deliverables, spanning engineering, permitting, construction, qualification and regulatory approval.

Phase One Scope and Timeline

  • Design and permitting (Q4 2026 - Q1 2027): engineering studies, architectural and structural design, and submission of the building permit application.
  • Quality control laboratory (Q1 - Q2 2027): construction of a new laboratory for quality control testing, followed by the transfer and qualification of laboratory instruments.
  • GMP warehouse (Q2 - Q3 2027): construction of a new warehouse in place of the existing warehouse, designed to improve the flow of materials into production, followed by qualification.
  • Regulatory inspection (Q3 2027): inspection by the EOF, targeted to complete the first phase.

Subsequent Phase

Following the first phase, the Master Plan provides for a dedicated powder production area within the facility. If completed and approved by the EOF, it would expand Cana's manufacturing portfolio with a purpose-built powder production capability, broadening the range of products available to contract manufacturing partners and to the Company's proprietary brands.

CEO Commentary

Greg Siokas, CEO of Cosmos Health, stated: "Our Facility Master Plan is designed to ensure that Cana's infrastructure keeps pace with the growth of its business. A new quality control laboratory and a new GMP warehouse form the foundation of the next stage of that growth, and we have a clear, structured plan in place, targeting completion by the third quarter of 2027.

"Together with our new capsule-filling line and tablet coating system, we believe these investments position Cana to serve more partners at higher volumes, while the planned powder production area would further expand its manufacturing capabilities."

About Cosmos Health Inc.

Cosmos Health Inc. (NASDAQ: COSM), incorporated in 2009 in Nevada, is a diversified, vertically integrated global healthcare group. The Company owns a portfolio of proprietary pharmaceutical and nutraceutical brands, including Sky Premium Life®, Mediterranation®, bio-bebe®, C-Sept® and C-Scrub®. Through its subsidiary Cana Laboratories S.A., licensed under European Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and certified by the European Medicines Agency (EMA), it manufactures pharmaceuticals, food supplements, cosmetics, biocides, and medical devices within the European Union. Cosmos Health also distributes a broad line of pharmaceuticals and parapharmaceuticals, including branded generics and OTC medications, to retail pharmacies and wholesale distributors through its subsidiaries in Greece and the UK. Furthermore, the Company has established R&D partnerships targeting major health disorders such as obesity, diabetes, and cancer, enhanced by artificial intelligence drug repurposing technologies, and focuses on the R&D of novel patented nutraceuticals, specialized root extracts, proprietary complex generics, and innovative OTC products. Cosmos Health has also entered the telehealth space through the acquisition of ZipDoctor, Inc., based in Texas, USA. With a global distribution platform, the Company is currently expanding throughout Europe, Asia, and North America, and has offices and distribution centers in Thessaloniki and Athens, Greece, and in Harlow, UK. NEW YORK CITY, NY / ACCESS Newswire / November 27, 2026 / The Age of Parity is no longer an abstract economic theory. It is becoming visible in real time.

A recent report in The New York Times examining the impact of surging fuel costs offers another reminder of how quickly an energy shock can become an economic shock. Recent fuel-price increases in Syria triggered widespread protests after diesel prices jumped 40 percent, while gasoline and other energy costs also increased sharply.

The circumstances in Syria are particular to that country. The larger economic lesson is not.

When oil becomes more expensive or difficult to obtain, the effects do not stop at the gas pump. They move through transportation, manufacturing, agriculture, packaging, logistics and eventually the price of everyday goods.

Plastic sits directly inside that equation.

Most conventional virgin plastic begins with fossil-fuel feedstocks. Its economics are therefore connected to a global system of oil and gas production, refining, transportation and trade. When that system becomes more expensive or unpredictable, manufacturers can feel the consequences far beyond the energy market.

That is why recycling plastic increasingly needs to be viewed as an economic strategy rather than simply an environmental objective.

SMX calls this shift the Age of Parity: the point at which the economics of recycled plastic begin competing more directly with the economics of virgin plastic.

For years, the conventional argument for recycling focused primarily on waste. Use less. Throw away less. Keep plastic out of landfills and oceans.

Those objectives remain important, but they no longer tell the whole story.

The economic argument may ultimately prove just as powerful.

Every tonne of usable plastic recovered from an existing waste stream represents material that potentially does not have to begin again with newly extracted fossil resources. Recycling creates the possibility of treating material already circulating through an economy as feedstock for the next generation of products.

That can turn waste into domestic inventory.

And in an era of volatile energy prices and disrupted supply chains, inventory matters.

THE NEW ECONOMICS OF PLASTIC

The Age of Parity changes the calculation because virgin plastic does not exist independently of the forces reshaping global energy markets.

Oil volatility and supply disruptions can affect the cost and availability of virgin material. Recycled plastic creates another potential supply source: material already contained in products, packaging and waste streams.

But for recycled plastic to function as a dependable industrial commodity, markets need more than supply. They need proof.

Manufacturers need to know what they are purchasing. Brands need evidence behind recycled-content claims. Regulators need information that can be audited. Buyers need a way to distinguish verified material from unsupported claims.

SMX's molecular marking and digital traceability technology is designed to give physical materials an identity that can remain connected to them through a supply chain. Molecular markers can be linked to digital records containing information about origin, composition and movement.

SMX's Digital Material Passport extends that identity into a digital record designed to travel with the material through its lifecycle. Instead of relying solely on paperwork or claims made at individual points in a supply chain, the passport is intended to connect physical plastic with information about what it is, where it came from and how it has moved through the system.

The company's Plastic Cycle Token (PCT)adds another component. It is designed to represent verified plastic-cycle activity digitally, connecting authenticated physical material with a tokenized record. Together, molecular identification, the Digital Material Passport and PCT are intended to create a bridge between physical recycling and the data needed to document it.

FROM WASTE STREAM TO SUPPLY STREAM

The Age of Parity reframes recycling from the final stop in a product's life to the beginning of another supply cycle.

Packaging, bottles, textiles and consumer products contain material that has already been manufactured. Recovering it does not eliminate the need for virgin plastic or insulate manufacturers from energy costs. It does create another potential source of raw material.

A manufacturer able to incorporate verified recycled material gains another procurement option. A country capable of recovering and reusing its plastic waste gains access to a material resource already within its borders.

The objective is not to declare recycled plastic universally cheaper than virgin plastic. Prices vary by polymer, geography, energy costs, processing requirements and market conditions. The larger change is that recycled plastic can increasingly be evaluated as an industrial input rather than simply an environmental substitute.

THE MATERIAL IS ALREADY HERE

Plastic presents an unusual opportunity because so much potential raw material is already in circulation. The question is whether economies can capture, identify and reuse it.

Technology alone cannot accomplish that. Collection systems, recycling infrastructure, manufacturers, regulators and markets all have roles to play. SMX's role is focused on identity and verification: connecting physical material with a record intended to remain useful as that material moves through successive cycles.

That matters because circularity ultimately depends on knowing what came back.

Plastic that can be recovered, identified, verified and reused is not merely waste diverted from a landfill. It is a resource that does not have to be created from scratch.

That is what the Age of Parity ultimately represents: not the end of virgin plastic or oil, but the emergence of a competing model in which yesterday's products can become tomorrow's raw materials.

In a world being reminded how quickly resource prices can change, throwing that material away is becoming increasingly difficult to justify.

ABOUT SMX (SECURITY MATTERS) PLC

SMX (Security Matters) PLC (NASDAQ:SMX) develops molecular traceability and material authentication technologies designed to strengthen supply-chain transparency and integrity across global industries. Its platform embeds invisible molecular markers directly into physical materials-including solids, liquids, and gases-allowing them to carry a persistent identity that can be detected and verified throughout their lifecycle.

Production, shipment and inventory figures are reported on a 100% Ramu basis. Nickel 28 currently holds an 8.56% joint-venture interest in Ramu which is operated by the Metallurgical Corporation of China ("MCC").

Q3 2026 Ramu Highlights:

  • Production of 9,043 tonnes of contained nickel in Mixed Hydroxide Precipitate ("MHP"), compared to 9,242 tonnes in the same period last year.
  • Production of 929 tonnes of contained cobalt in MHP, compared to 887 tonnes in the same period last year.
  • Nickel sales of 7,403 tonnes of contained nickel, compared to 9,880 tonnes in the same period last year.
  • Cobalt sales of 775 tonnes of contained cobalt, compared to 948 tonnes in the same period last year.
  • Nickel inventory on hand at quarter-end was 2,734 tonnes of nickel in MHP, compared to 1,094 tonnes at June 30, 2026.
  • London Metal Exchange average nickel price of US$7.52/lb in Q3 2026, an increase of 10% from the same period last year (US$6.81/lb).
  • Average cobalt price of US$24.41/lb in Q3 2026, an increase of 58% from the same period last year (US$15.48/lb).
  • Production costs, net of by-product credits were US$6.15/lb of nickel produced in MHP, compared to US$3.07/lb in the same period last year, primarily reflecting higher sulphur prices. Year-to-date 2026 production costs, net of by-product credits, were US$4.25/lb of nickel produced in MHP, compared to US$3.27/lb in the same period last year.

Nickel 28's Chief Executive Officer, Craig Lennon stated: "Ramu continued to deliver strong operational performance during the third quarter of 2026, with nickel and cobalt production remaining robust and the project continuing to demonstrate its operational reliability. While reported sales volumes were lower than the previous quarter, this was principally attributable to the timing of a shipment that was not recognised within the quarter. As a result, inventory levels increased at quarter end, and we expect this timing difference to reverse in the following quarter. Importantly, the lower sales volumes do not reflect any deterioration in underlying production performance.

The operating environment has, however, become increasingly challenging, with a significant increase in production costs during the quarter, driven primarily by the continued escalation in sulphur prices. Sulphur is a major consumable in the high-pressure acid leach (HPAL) process, and the sustained increase in its price has had a material impact on operating costs and margins. These cost pressures have been compounded by lower average nickel and cobalt prices during the quarter, resulting in a more difficult financial environment than we experienced during the first half of 2026.

Nickel prices softened during the quarter, reflecting continued concerns regarding global oversupply, particularly from Indonesia. Cobalt prices also weakened as increased availability of material from the Democratic Republic of Congo and subdued downstream demand placed pressure on the market. The combination of lower commodity prices and higher input costs has resulted in a significant compression of operating margins, despite the continued strong production performance at Ramu.

Looking ahead, Indonesian governmental policy remains a critical factor in determining the direction of global nickel prices. In particular, the Indonesian government's management of nickel ore production quotas through its Work Plan and Budget (Rencana Kerja dan Anggaran Biaya, or RKAB) approval process will be closely watched by the industry. The RKAB is the mandatory annual operational and financial blueprint that mining license holders must get approved by the Indonesian Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources or relevant local governor before carrying out exploration or production activities. Recent indications that Indonesia may adopt a more restrictive approach to production quotas in 2027 are encouraging and could help address the current global supply imbalance. However, the extent and timing of any resulting improvement in nickel prices remain uncertain.

While we remain confident in the underlying operational performance of Ramu, we expect the challenging cost and commodity price environment to continue to impact profitability and cash generation in the near term. The focus for the project remains on maintaining strong production performance, managing operating costs where possible and positioning the project to benefit from any improvement in market conditions."

Salt Lake City, Utah, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- TruGolf Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: TRUG), today announced a 1-for-5 reverse split of its Class A common stock. The reverse stock split was approved by the Company’s Board of Directors in accordance with Section 78.207 of the Nevada Revised Statutes and is intended to enable the Company to regain compliance with the $1.00 minimum bid price requirement for continued listing on The Nasdaq Capital Market. Beginning on December 1, 2026, the Company’s Class A common stock will continue to trade on The Nasdaq Capital Market on a split adjusted basis under the trading symbol “TRUG” but will trade under the following new CUSIP number: 243733706.

As a result of the reverse stock split, every 5 shares of Class A common stock issued and outstanding as of the effective date will be automatically combined into one share of Class A common stock. No fractional shares will be issued if, as a result of the reverse stock split, a stockholder would otherwise become entitled to a fractional share because the number of shares of Class A common stock they hold before the reverse stock split is not evenly divisible by the split ratio. Instead, each stockholder will be entitled to receive a cash payment in lieu of a fractional share.

The reverse stock split will reduce the number of shares of outstanding Class A common stock from approximately 2.9 million shares, the number of shares outstanding as of the date hereof, to approximately 0.57 million shares. The par value of the Class A common stock will remain unchanged and the number of authorized shares of Class A common stock will be proportionately reduced to 2 million shares. The reverse split affects all stockholders uniformly and will not alter any common stockholder’s percentage interest in the Company’s equity, except to the extent that the reverse split results in some common stockholders owning a fractional share as described above.

Toronto, Ontario and Geraldton, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Tombill Mines Limited (TSXV: TBLL) (the "Company", "Tombill"), is pleased to announce that it has appointed Ashley Nadon as its new Chief Financial Officer.

Ms. Nadon is a Chartered Professional Accountant with extensive experience providing financial management, accounting and regulatory compliance services to publicly traded companies. Founded in 1935 by Newmont Mining and 'Tom' and 'Bill' Johnson, Tombill Mines Limited (TSXV: TBLL) owns 2 of the 11 past-producing and producing mines in Geraldton, in the Greenstone gold district (pop. 4,300, approximately 225 km northeast of Thunder Bay). Within this established local and mining infrastructure, its assets comprise four claim groups, most of which strategically occupy the middle of the Geraldton gold district. Its claims sit on a shared boundary with, and down plunge from, the open pit of Equinox Gold's Greenstone Gold Mine (first gold pour May 2024), one of Canada's largest long-life gold mines and mills by annual production.

Perth, Western Australia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Besra Gold Inc. (ASX: BEZ) ("Besra" or the "Company") reminds shareholders that its annual general and special meeting ("AGM") is scheduled to be held in Toronto on 7 December 2026. Participation by all shareholders is particularly important this year, as the AGM is being held in the context of sustained efforts by a group of minority shareholders to reconstitute the Company's board of directors (the "Board"). Your vote is crucial to support the incumbent members of the Board and the positive momentum that is building at Besra.

Since shareholders voted to reconstitute the Board at the special meeting held on 23 June 2025, a group of minority shareholders of the Company (the "Dissident Group") have repeatedly sought to replace or constrain the Board, including by attempting to requisition shareholder meetings on at least seven occasions, soliciting support from select shareholders without making public disclosure available to all shareholders, and most recently, purporting to nominate a slate of directors for election at the AGM. These efforts have repeatedly failed to comply with applicable law and the Company's constating documents. Throughout, the Company has engaged with members of the Dissident Group and encouraged them to pursue their objectives through proper legal channels available to shareholders. It is in this context that the Company will hold its fifth shareholder meeting in approximately two years.

Purported Director Nominations

On 6 November 2026, the Company received a notice from a member of the Dissident Group purporting to nominate four individuals for election at the AGM, two of whom have already been rejected by shareholders of the Company at past shareholder meetings:

(1) Mr David Potter, who briefly served as Chair of the Board from 19 May 2025 until he was removed by shareholders on 23 June 2025. Mr Potter was narrowly elected to the Board again on 15 December 2025, before again being removed by shareholders on 16 June 2026.

(2) Mr Matthew Antill, who previously served as managing director of a subsidiary of the Company, until being made redundant from that role effective 22 December 2025. Mr Antill recently stood for election at the meeting of shareholders held on 16 June 2026 and was not elected.

(3) Mr Brady Jausel, a member of the Dissident Group who has repeatedly sought to requisition shareholder meetings to replace the Board and is now proposed to join the Board himself.

(4) Ms Joanna Line-Jollymore, a Canadian elementary school teacher, who was added as a nominee after the Company advised the Dissident Group of the Canadian director requirements that apply to the Company.

The Board has reviewed the director nominations and has concluded that they were not made in compliance with the Company's advance notice by-law. Under the by-law, only persons nominated in accordance with its procedures are eligible for election as directors. The advance notice by-law is similar to by-laws adopted by many other Canadian public companies and is intended to ensure that shareholders are provided with relevant disclosure about persons proposed for election as directors.

The Company's legal counsel wrote to the nominating shareholder on 11 November 2026 setting out the deficiencies in its purported nominations. As of the date of this announcement, the Company has not received a response.

Lack of Disclosure to Shareholders

The nomination notice submitted to the Company lists fourteen individuals who are identified as joint actors in connection with the nominations, many of whom participated in the Dissident Group's previous attempts to replace the Board. Despite this private acknowledgement, the Dissident Group has made no public disclosure regarding its existence, its members, the extent of their interests in Besra, or their intentions for the Company should they succeed in replacing the Board. Instead, it has been brought to the Company's attention that members of the Dissident Group have contacted other shareholders of the Company directly to solicit their support.

The Company has significant concerns that the Dissident Group is effectively conducting a shadow proxy contest, privately seeking the support of select shareholders, rather than making public disclosure to all shareholders and seeking their support in accordance with applicable law and established procedures for shareholders seeking to reconstitute a board of directors. The Company has repeatedly encouraged members of the Dissident Group to obtain legal advice and to comply with applicable laws. These concerns have been brought to the attention of Canadian securities regulators.

Shareholders who are contacted by members of the Dissident Group or persons acting on their behalf are encouraged to exercise caution and to rely on the Company's public disclosure, which is available under the Company's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca.

Message from the Chair

Commenting on the purported nominations, Besra Chairman Dr John Blake said:

"The Board recognises that voting at the Company's recent shareholder meetings reflects a range of sincerely held views regarding the future direction of Besra. Differences of opinion are not unusual in a public company, and the Board values engaged shareholders who care deeply about the future of Besra and the value of their investment. While shareholders may hold differing views on aspects of strategy, governance or execution, I believe all parties share a common objective: to maximise the long-term value of Besra's assets and position the Company for sustainable success."

"The latest nominations, however, continue a campaign of destabilisation that is counter to that objective. The current Board has worked tirelessly to address a number of significant legacy issues that have affected the Company and to establish a pathway to develop the Bau Gold Project in a manner that is responsible, sustainable, and that restores value for our shareholders. Tenure, feasibility, and funding are the cornerstones of responsible project development, and they must apply in the case of Bau. There are no shortcuts available. These objectives – tenure, feasibility and funding – have been a focus of the current Board, which believes that responsible governance is necessary to build the trust and confidence of stakeholders, including key decision makers in the Sarawak Government."

"What is important now is that Besra moves forward constructively in the best interests of all shareholders. Recurring campaigns of this kind that repeatedly propose leadership changes that shareholders have previously declined to endorse are a counterproductive diversion of resources and attention at a time when the Company and its Board need to focus on creating shareholder value. Following the AGM, we hope that all shareholders, including the members of the Dissident Group, will remain constructively engaged while supporting a period of stability that allows the Board to build on the Company's momentum in its next stages of growth. To that end, the Board unanimously encourages shareholders to vote FOR the re-election of each of the incumbent directors at the AGM."

Deadline to Vote

CDI holders must submit voting instruction forms no later than 9:00 a.m. (Perth, Australia time) on 2 December 2026 or no later than four full business days before any adjournment or postponement of the AGM. Proxies must be submitted by 9:00 a.m. (Perth, Australia time) on 4 December 2026 or no later than 48 hours prior to any adjournment or postponement of the AGM. For additional information regarding the AGM, shareholders are encouraged to review the Company's management information circular dated 20 October 2026, which is available under the Company's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca.
